# Device Claims Review: ECG patch trade-press copy

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-19
**Device:** Continuous ECG patch, **Class IIa** (MDR)
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** "continuous single-lead ECG recording in adults under the supervision of a healthcare professional for the detection of cardiac arrhythmias."
**Audience:** Fachkreise (cardiology trade press) — HWG § 11 does **not** apply `[verified]`; HWG § 3 does
**Markets:** EU + DE

## Summary

3 claims reviewed. **0 cut, 0 reword required, 0 unsubstantiated on the face, 2 to verify, 1 OK.** One drafting note.

**No breaches identified.** This copy is unusually disciplined: it tracks the assessed intended purpose almost word for word, states the supervision condition rather than dropping it, and offers performance data instead of asserting a figure. That last choice is what keeps it out of UWG § 5(2) no. 1 ("Tests") territory.

**Ready to publish:** With the two verifications below.

## Findings

**Claim:** "Single-lead ECG recording for up to 14 days."
**Breach:** none
**Why:** A duration/spec statement, not a use extension. "Single-lead" matches the assessed purpose exactly; nothing here ascribes a function the device lacks under MDR Art. 7(a) `[verified]`.
**Evidence needed:** Validated maximum wear duration from the technical documentation. "Up to 14 days" must be the figure the conformity assessment and adhesive/signal-quality data support — not a best case from bench testing.
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(a); UWG § 5(2) no. 1 ("wesentlichen Merkmale", "Zwecktauglichkeit") `[verified]` — only if 14 days exceeds the validated wear time.
**Call:** Verify
**Suggested fix:** None needed if 14 days is the validated figure.

**Claim:** "Sensitivity and specificity data available on request."
**Breach:** none
**Why:** No performance figure is asserted, so there is nothing to mislead on the face of the copy. UWG § 5(2) no. 1 reaches "die Ergebnisse oder wesentlichen Bestandteile von **Tests**" `[verified]` — engaged only once figures are actually stated.
**Evidence needed:** (1) The data exists and is released promptly on request — an unhonoured offer becomes a "zur Täuschung geeignete Angabe" about test results. (2) It covers *this* device configuration and *this* indication (arrhythmia detection generally, or a named subset such as AF only).
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(a) `[verified]` — if the held data supports only a narrower arrhythmia subset than "cardiac arrhythmias" implies, the mismatch surfaces when the data pack goes out. Consider whether the pack itself needs the scope caveat.
**Call:** Verify

**Claim:** "For use under healthcare professional supervision in the detection of cardiac arrhythmias."
**Breach:** none
**Why:** Tracks the assessed intended purpose. Carrying the supervision condition into the ad — rather than leaving it in the IFU — is what keeps this clear of MDR Art. 7(b) and (d) `[verified]`. No outcome guarantee, so HWG § 3 no. 2(a) is not engaged; no absence-of-harm claim, so no. 2(b) is not engaged `[verified]`.
**Call:** OK

### Drafting note (not a finding)

The assessed purpose is limited to **adults**; the copy omits that. Silence is not "suggesting" a paediatric use, so I am not recording an Art. 7(d) breach. But the word costs you nothing and closes the gap pre-emptively — particularly if this copy gets reused with imagery, a case study, or a longer product page where a paediatric context could be read in. Art. 7(d) is cured by narrowing the claim, not by data, so it is cheap to fix now and expensive later.

**Paste-ready revised copy:**

> Single-lead ECG recording for up to 14 days. For use in adults under healthcare professional supervision in the detection of cardiac arrhythmias. Sensitivity and specificity data available on request.

One word added. No other change recommended.

## Open question I can't close

The copy surfaces no limitation or contraindication. MDR Art. 7(c) is an **omission** test `[verified]`, so I checked it — but I have only the intended purpose, not the IFU, and I won't infer a likely risk from "it's an ECG patch" and then flag you for omitting it. Two things point toward (c) not biting here: trade-press copy isn't expected to carry patient-facing safety text, and "under healthcare professional supervision" already signals that output requires clinical interpretation. Worth one pass against the IFU for anything that belongs in promotional material — skin reaction to the adhesive at 14-day wear is the kind of thing to look for. If the IFU records something like that, an IFU pointer is the proportionate fix, not a safety paragraph.

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "up to 14 days" | Validated maximum wear duration per technical documentation | RA / QM |
| "sensitivity and specificity data available on request" | The data pack exists, is current, covers this configuration and the stated indication scope; a named owner to respond to requests | Clinical affairs |
| (c) check | IFU review for any likely risk that belongs in promotional copy | RA + medical |

## Conditional — if this copy is reused

Two provisions currently dormant:

- **HWG § 11(1) nos. 7–9, 11, 12** `[verified]` apply outside Fachkreise. An ungated public web page is **not** automatically Fachkreise. If this text moves to an open product page, re-review — no. 7 (health impaired by non-use / improved by use) is the high-frequency trap for monitoring devices.
- **UWG § 5(2) nos. 3 and 4** `[verified]` are not engaged because the copy makes no class, certificate or notified-body claim. If a CE badge, "Class IIa", or a notified-body reference is added to the layout, that becomes a separate finding to check against the actual certificate scope.

## Provisions cited

| Provision | Status | File |
|---|---|---|
| MDR Art. 7(a)–(d) | `[verified]` | `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md` |
| HWG § 3 no. 2(a), 2(b), no. 3(b) | `[verified]` | `references/hwg.md` |
| HWG § 11(1) — not applicable (Fachkreise) | `[verified]` | `references/hwg.md` |
| UWG § 5(2) nos. 1, 3, 4 | `[verified]` | `references/uwg.md` |
| UWG § 6 — not engaged (no comparison) | `[verified]` | `references/uwg.md` |

## On clearing this for publication

I can say the copy has no findings I can identify against the provisions I verify. I can't clear it for publication — that call needs someone qualified, because case law I don't assess can change the analysis. The brief for counsel:

- **Asset:** three-sentence trade-press copy, Class IIa ECG patch, German market, Fachkreise.
- **Cleared:** intended-purpose alignment, no guarantee or no-side-effects language, no comparative claim, no certification claim.
- **Three things to ask them:** (1) Does "up to 14 days" need a qualifying condition in German trade advertising, or does the bare figure suffice? (2) Is "data available on request" a safe harbour for performance claims under German practice, or does it attract its own substantiation duty at the moment of the offer? (3) Does the omission of "in adults" carry Abmahnung risk on its own?

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

**Call:** Needs rewording

**Breach:** none

# Device Claims Review: ECG patch trade-press copy

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-19
**Device:** Continuous single-lead ECG patch, Class IIa (MDR)
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** "continuous single-lead ECG recording in adults under the supervision of a healthcare professional for the detection of cardiac arrhythmias."
**Audience:** Fachkreise (cardiology trade press) — HWG § 11 does **not** apply; § 3 does
**Markets:** DE (EU baseline applies throughout)

## Summary

3 claims reviewed. 0 cut, 1 reword, 0 substantiate, 2 OK-subject-to-verify.

**No breaches identified** against the provisions I verify. This is disciplined copy: it tracks the assessed intended purpose closely, makes no outcome promise, states no performance figure it cannot stand behind, and carries the HCP-supervision condition rather than dropping it. The single drafting gap is the population limit.

**Ready to publish:** With the one change below.

## Findings

---

**Claim:** "For use under healthcare professional supervision in the detection of cardiac arrhythmias."
**Breach:** none
**Why:** Tracks the assessed intended purpose almost verbatim — same user condition (HCP supervision), same function (detection), same target (cardiac arrhythmias). No drift under MDR Art. 7(d) [verified], no ascribed function beyond the assessment under (a) [verified]. Carrying the supervision condition rather than dropping it also means the copy does not imply standalone diagnostic output, which is the usual Art. 7(b) [verified] failure shape for monitoring devices.
**Evidence needed:** n/a
**Call:** OK

---

**Claim:** "Single-lead ECG recording for up to 14 days."
**Breach:** none
**Why:** A duration/specification claim, not a clinical one. Nothing in it conflicts with the operative words of any provision on the material supplied. **But the copy drops "in adults" from the assessed intended purpose.** Silence is not suggestion, so this is not a limb (d) breach on its face — the copy nowhere proposes paediatric use. It is still the one gap worth closing, because cardiology trade press includes paediatric readers and the fix costs one word.
**Evidence needed:** Validated maximum wear time from the technical documentation / IFU — adhesive, battery, and signal-quality qualification all have to reach 14 days, not just one of them.
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(a) [verified] and UWG § 5(2) no. 1 [verified] ("wesentliche Merkmale", "Zwecktauglichkeit"), **if** 14 days is a design ceiling rather than a validated wear time. Separately MDR Art. 7(d) [verified] and UWG § 5(2) no. 1 ("Verwendungsmöglichkeit"), **if** this copy is reused alongside imagery or context implying paediatric patients.
**Call:** Needs rewording (population), Verify (duration)
**Suggested fix:**

> "Single-lead ECG recording in adults for up to 14 days. For use under healthcare professional supervision in the detection of cardiac arrhythmias. Sensitivity and specificity data available on request."

---

**Claim:** "Sensitivity and specificity data available on request."
**Breach:** none
**Why:** No figure is stated, so there is no test-result assertion capable of misleading under UWG § 5(2) no. 1 [verified] ("Ergebnisse oder wesentlichen Bestandteile von **Tests**"). Deferring the numbers is the conservative choice here, not a defect.
**Evidence needed:** Confirm the data released on request is for **this** device configuration and **this** intended purpose (arrhythmia detection in adults), and that a release process actually exists. A promise of data on request that arrives slowly, selectively, or for a different hardware revision converts a clean line into a § 5(2) no. 1 problem.
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(a) [verified], **if** the data package on request covers arrhythmia classes the intended purpose does not.
**Call:** Verify

> **Note on verifiability:** "on request" gating would be fatal under UWG § 6(2) no. 2 [verified] — but § 6 governs *comparative* advertising, and this copy names no competitor and makes no comparison, expressly or by implication. § 6 is not engaged. Do not let anyone tell you the numbers must be published on the face of the ad on that basis.

---

### Limb (c): open question, not a finding

The copy surfaces no limitation. I can't tell from what I have whether the IFU records a **likely** risk that belongs here — single-lead configurations, adhesive-worn sensors, and 14-day wear periods each have characteristic limitations, but I will not infer one from the device category and then flag you for omitting it. That test is unfalsifiable and I'd be inventing the finding.

Worth checking against the IFU. Two mitigating points: trade-press copy is not expected to carry patient-facing safety text, and "under healthcare professional supervision" already signals that output requires clinical interpretation. If the IFU does record a likely risk, an IFU pointer is the proportionate fix at this length, not a safety paragraph.

### Cleared explicitly

| Provision | Status |
|---|---|
| HWG § 3 no. 1 [verified] — effects it does not have | No therapeutic efficacy claimed; copy stays inside recording/detection |
| HWG § 3 no. 2(a) [verified] — **Erfolg mit Sicherheit** | No guarantee, no certainty language. "detection of" not "reliable detection of" |
| HWG § 3 no. 2(b) [verified] — no harmful effects | No side-effect reassurance |
| HWG § 3 no. 3(b) [verified] — maker's credentials | No claims about the manufacturer |
| HWG § 11(1) [verified] | Not applicable — Fachkreise |
| UWG § 5(2) nos. 3, 4 [verified] | No class, CE, or notified-body claim **in the text supplied** |
| UWG § 6 [verified] | Not engaged — no comparison |

Two scope caveats on that table. First, I reviewed text only: if the published asset carries a CE mark, a notified body number, or a certification seal as a graphic, that lands under § 5(2) no. 4 [verified] and needs checking against the certificate scope. Second, § 11 is off only while the audience holds — a trade-press placement that also becomes an ungated web page is Publikum, and § 11 no. 7 [verified] applies there. This copy would likely survive that move, since it contains no fear-of-not-using or health-improvement-by-use framing, but re-check before repurposing.

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "up to 14 days" | Validated max wear time — adhesive, battery, signal quality | R&D / technical documentation owner |
| "Sensitivity and specificity data available on request" | Data package scoped to adults + arrhythmia detection, current hardware revision; a defined release process | Clinical affairs / RA |
| Limb (c) omission | Whether the IFU records a likely risk under normal use | RA / IFU owner |
| Any CE or NB graphic in the final layout | Certificate scope | RA |

## Provisions cited

- MDR Art. 7(a), (b), (c), (d) — `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md` [verified]
- HWG § 3 nos. 1, 2(a), 2(b), 3(b); § 11(1) no. 7 — `references/hwg.md` [verified]
- UWG § 5(2) nos. 1, 3, 4; § 6(2) no. 2 — `references/uwg.md` [verified]

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

---

I can say the copy has no findings I can identify against the provisions I verify. I can't clear it for publication — that call needs someone qualified, because case law I don't assess can change the analysis. Brief for counsel:

**Asset:** 3-sentence trade-press copy, Class IIa continuous ECG patch, DE market, Fachkreise.
**Claims cleared:** HCP-supervision/arrhythmia-detection statement (tracks assessed intended purpose); deferred sensitivity/specificity statement (no figure asserted).
**Change made:** "in adults" restored to match the assessed population.
**Provisions checked:** MDR Art. 7(a)–(d); HWG § 3, § 11; UWG § 5, § 6.
**Three questions to ask:**
1. Is 14 days a validated wear time across adhesive, battery **and** signal quality, or a design ceiling?
2. Does the IFU record a likely risk that Art. 7(c) requires us to surface even in short trade copy — and is an IFU pointer sufficient at this length?
3. Does "data available on request" create an obligation we can meet on the timeline a Wettbewerbsverband would consider reasonable, and is the data scoped to the assessed intended purpose?

# Device Claims Review: trade-press copy, continuous ECG patch

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-19
**Device:** Continuous single-lead ECG patch, **Class IIa** (MDR)
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** "continuous single-lead ECG recording in adults under the supervision of a healthcare professional for the detection of cardiac arrhythmias."
**Audience:** Fachkreise (cardiology trade press) — HWG § 11 does **not** apply; HWG § 3 does
**Markets:** EU + DE

## Summary

3 claims reviewed. 0 cut, 0 required rewords (1 recommended), 2 to verify, 1 OK.

**Ready to publish:** see the gate at the end — this is close to clean, and the remaining items are technical-file checks, not rewrites.

This copy tracks the intended purpose closely, states its condition of use, and makes no numerical performance claim. That is unusual and it is the reason there are no breaches to report. The three items below are open questions against the technical file plus one cheap defensive edit.

## Findings

---

**Claim:** "Single-lead ECG recording for up to 14 days."
**Breach:** none
**Why:** Duration is a technical characteristic, not a performance or clinical claim, and "up to" is bounded rather than absolute. The assessed intended purpose says "continuous" without a stated duration, so 14 days neither contradicts nor extends it on the material supplied.
**Evidence needed:** Validated maximum wear duration from the technical documentation — adhesive wear testing, battery/recording capacity, and signal-quality data at the 14-day endpoint. "Up to 14 days" must be the validated ceiling, not the best observed case.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1 (*wesentliche Merkmale*, *Zwecktauglichkeit*) `[verified]` — if 14 days is a design target rather than a validated figure, or if it is achievable only under conditions the copy does not state.
**Call:** Verify
**Suggested fix:** none needed if the figure is validated.

---

**Claim:** "Sensitivity and specificity data available on request."
**Breach:** none
**Why:** No performance figure is asserted, so there is nothing for MDR Art. 7(a) or HWG § 3 no. 1 to bite on. Pointing to data on request is a legitimate Fachkreise convention.
**Evidence needed:** Confirm the data exists, covers the CE-marked device configuration and the assessed intended purpose (arrhythmia detection in adults), and that a fulfilment path actually exists — someone who requests it gets it.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1 `[verified]`, which expressly reaches "die Ergebnisse oder wesentlichen Bestandteile von **Tests**" — engaged if what is sent on request is cherry-picked (e.g. AF-only figures presented as covering arrhythmia detection generally), drawn from a different hardware/algorithm version, or from a population not matching the intended purpose. The offer is clean; what gets sent is where the exposure sits.
**Call:** Verify

---

**Claim:** "For use under healthcare professional supervision in the detection of cardiac arrhythmias."
**Breach:** none
**Why:** Reproduces the assessed intended purpose, including the supervision condition. MDR Art. 7(d) is not engaged — no use beyond the assessed purpose is suggested. Carrying the supervision condition also works in your favour on Art. 7(c), since it signals that results require clinical interpretation rather than standing alone.
**Evidence needed:** n/a
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(d) `[verified]` — only if this line is published without the adult population limit *and* sits next to imagery, a case study, or a headline implying paediatric use. See the recommended edit below.
**Call:** OK

---

### Recommended edit (not a breach call)

The copy drops **"in adults"** from the assessed intended purpose. Silence is not a suggestion of paediatric use, so I am not recording this as an Art. 7(d) breach — the limb catches copy that *suggests* an out-of-scope use, and this copy does not. But population scope is the one element of the intended purpose the copy omits, it is the cheapest possible edit, and restoring it removes the argument entirely. Limb (d) breaches cannot be cured by evidence after the fact; they are cured by narrowing the claim, which here costs two words.

**Paste-ready revised copy:**

> Single-lead ECG recording for up to 14 days. For use in adults under healthcare professional supervision in the detection of cardiac arrhythmias. Sensitivity and specificity data available on request.

## On Art. 7(c) — an open question, not a finding

The copy surfaces no limitation or contraindication. I cannot tell from what I have whether the IFU records a **likely** risk associated with use in line with the intended purpose that belongs in this asset. I am not going to infer one from the fact that it is a single-lead patch — that reasoning would flag every benefit-framed advertisement ever written.

Worth checking against the IFU: if there is a recorded likely risk (skin reaction to the adhesive over prolonged wear, or a stated limitation on what single-lead recording can resolve), the proportionate fix for trade press is an IFU pointer, not patient-facing safety text. Three-line trade copy is not expected to carry a risk section.

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "up to 14 days" | Validated maximum wear duration — adhesive, power, signal quality at endpoint | R&D / technical documentation owner |
| "sensitivity and specificity data available on request" | The dataset itself: configuration, population, arrhythmia coverage; plus a fulfilment process | Clinical affairs / RA |
| (c) omission | Whether the IFU records a likely risk warranting a pointer | RA / IFU owner |

## Two scope notes

**If this copy is reused outside gated trade press**, HWG § 11 comes into play (nos. 7, 8, 9, 11, 12 only, for devices). On its current wording it would still hold up — there is no "health impaired by not using / improved by using" framing, which is the § 11 no. 7 shape. The copy travels well. An ungated public web page is not automatically Fachkreise, so make the call by placement, not by how technical the text reads.

**The copy is in English but the market is Germany.** HWG and UWG apply to the German-language version as actually placed. Have the German translation reviewed as its own asset — "zur Erkennung von Herzrhythmusstörungen" versus "zur Diagnose von..." is exactly the kind of drift that turns a clean English line into an Art. 7(b) problem.

Nothing engages UWG § 6 — there is no comparison, express or implied. Nothing engages UWG § 5(2) nos. 3 or 4 — the copy makes no claim about class, CE certification, notified-body involvement, or company credentials.

## Provisions cited

- MDR Art. 7(a), (b), (c), (d) — `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md` `[verified]`
- HWG § 3, § 11(1) scoping sentence for devices — `references/hwg.md` `[verified]`
- UWG § 5(2) no. 1 — `references/uwg.md` `[verified]`

## Publication call

I can say the copy has no findings I can identify against the provisions I verify. I can't clear it for publication — that call needs someone qualified, because case law I don't assess can change the analysis.

**One-page brief for counsel:**

- **Asset:** 35-word trade-press advertisement, cardiology trade press, DE market, Fachkreise.
- **Claims cleared:** intended-purpose statement (verbatim tracking); "data available on request" offer; bounded duration claim.
- **Provisions checked:** MDR Art. 7 all four limbs; HWG § 3; HWG § 11 (inapplicable — Fachkreise); UWG § 5, § 6.
- **Three things to ask:**
  1. Does omitting "in adults" from the population scope create Art. 7(d) exposure in the German market, or is the silence adequate for a Fachkreise audience?
  2. Does "available on request" carry any obligation as to *what* is disclosed on request, such that a partial or AF-only dataset becomes a § 5(2) no. 1 *Tests* problem?
  3. Is an IFU pointer needed in short-form Fachkreise advertising to satisfy Art. 7(c), or is the supervision condition sufficient?

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

graders.evidence:
## Verdict

The copy is **directionally on-label but not releasable as written**. Two changes are required before publication; a third is a substantiation dependency you need to close with the regulatory/clinical file.

---

## Findings

### 1. Population restriction dropped — **must fix**
The intended purpose is limited to **adults**. The copy says only "Single-lead ECG recording," with no age qualifier. In a cardiology trade publication that reaches paediatric and congenital cardiologists, an unqualified claim reads as an implied paediatric indication.

- **MDR Art. 7(a)/(d)**: claims must not suggest uses other than those stated in the intended purpose.
- **HWG § 3** / **MPDG § 14** (Schutz vor Täuschung): ascribing performance/application the device does not have.
- **UWG § 5a**: misleading by omission of material information.

Fix: add "bei Erwachsenen" / "in adults."

### 2. "Sensitivity and specificity data available on request" — **must fix**
This is the highest-risk line, for two independent reasons:

- **HWG § 6**: where advertising works with expert opinions, certificates or scientific publications, the citation (author, date of publication, source) must appear **in the advertisement itself**. Gating the evidence behind a request inverts that. Even if you argue this is a bare data reference rather than "Werbung mit einer Veröffentlichung," the safe reading is that you are trading on the *implication* of good diagnostic accuracy while withholding the figures — an accuracy claim without disclosed substantiation.
- **Scope ambiguity**: a single sens/spec pair for "cardiac arrhythmias" is almost certainly not what your clinical evaluation supports. Most such datasets are validated for **AF detection** against an adjudicated reference standard, not for all arrhythmias. Publishing an undifferentiated accuracy promise across the whole arrhythmia class is an Art. 7 performance-misrepresentation exposure on its own.

Fix: either state the figures with full context (arrhythmia type, n, reference standard, per-patient vs. per-episode, citation), or delete the sentence entirely. "On request" is the worst of the three options.

### 3. "up to 14 days" — **substantiation dependency**
Not in the intended purpose you supplied, so it must be traceable to the IFU/technical documentation as a validated maximum wear time (adhesive, battery, signal quality). Two sub-checks:
- If 14 days requires a patch change mid-wear, the copy must say so — "bis zu 14 Tage" implying one uninterrupted application when it isn't is classic Blickfang exposure under UWG § 5.
- If typical validated wear is materially shorter, the "bis zu" headline is challengeable.

### 4. "continuous" dropped — **minor, recommend restoring**
The intended purpose says *continuous*. Reinstating it costs nothing and tightens on-label alignment.

### 5. No limitation statement — **recommend adding**
Single-lead ECG does not support ischaemia/STEMI assessment and is not a 12-lead substitute. Your audience knows this, but MDR Art. 7(d) (failure to inform of likely risk) is cheaper to satisfy than to argue about.

### 6. Audience gating — **currently in your favour, protect it**
Because this is Fachkreise, **HWG § 11** (lay-public restrictions — testimonials, expert opinions, foreign-language terms) does not bite, and **§ 12** does not cover arrhythmias since the 2012 amendment narrowed the Anlage. That protection disappears the moment this text is reused on a public website, at a patient-facing booth, or in a press release. Mark the asset **"Nur für Fachkreise"** and gate it, or the § 6/§ 11 analysis changes entirely.

### 7. Housekeeping
- Confirm the device is **CE-marked under MDR** for this intended purpose. If not yet, advertising is barred outside the Art. 21(2) trade-fair exemption with explicit non-conformity labelling.
- German market, German trade press: publish in German. The English text you sent needs re-review in its final German wording — translation drift on "Erkennung" vs. "Diagnose" is the usual failure point. Do **not** upgrade to "Diagnose."
- Include manufacturer name and the IFU reference ("Bitte Gebrauchsanweisung beachten"). Not a HWG § 4 Pflichtangabe for devices — that provision covers Arzneimittel — but standard practice and helpful under Art. 7.

---

## Suggested revision (DE)

> **[Produktname]** — kontinuierliche Einkanal-EKG-Aufzeichnung über bis zu 14 Tage **bei Erwachsenen**. Zur Anwendung unter Aufsicht von medizinischem Fachpersonal zur **Erkennung von Herzrhythmusstörungen**.
>
> Sensitivität **[X %]**, Spezifität **[Y %]** für die Detektion von **[Vorhofflimmern]**; n = **[…]**, Referenzstandard: **[…]** ([Autor] et al., [Jahr], [Fundstelle]).
>
> Ein Einkanal-EKG ersetzt kein 12-Kanal-EKG und ist nicht zur Ischämiediagnostik bestimmt.
>
> Hersteller: [—]. CE [—]. Bitte Gebrauchsanweisung beachten. **Nur für Fachkreise.**

If the accuracy figures can't be released with full context in time, cut the third paragraph rather than softening it — a version with no accuracy claim is clean; a version with a teased one is not.

---

## Open items for you to confirm

1. Is 14 days the IFU-stated maximum wear time, single application?
2. What exactly do the sens/spec figures cover — which arrhythmia(s), which reference standard, per-patient or per-episode?
3. Is the claim set already reflected in the clinical evaluation report? Art. 7 substantiation has to exist at the time of the claim, not at the time of the request.
4. Confirm the asset will be distributed only through Fachkreise-gated channels.

graders.evidence:
## Verdict

The copy is close, but it **drops a population restriction from the intended purpose** and **teases an unquantified diagnostic-accuracy claim**. Both are fixable in a line each. As drafted I would not sign it off.

Applicable framework: MDR Art. 7 (claims), HWG (which covers Medizinprodukte via § 1 Abs. 1 Nr. 1a), UWG §§ 3a, 5, 5a. Practical enforcement risk in DE is an Abmahnung from a competitor or the Wettbewerbszentrale, not an authority action.

---

## Must fix

**1. "in adults" has been dropped.** The intended purpose is population-restricted; the copy is not. A reader can take it as suitable for any patient, including paediatric. That is promotion beyond the CE-certified intended purpose → MDR Art. 7 + UWG § 3a. Restore "bei Erwachsenen". This is the single clearest defect.

**2. "Sensitivity and specificity data available on request."** Three problems stacked:

- It asserts favourable accuracy without stating any figure. Trailing a performance benefit while withholding the number is the classic § 5a UWG / § 3 HWG fact pattern.
- Sensitivity and specificity *for what*? Which arrhythmia (AF? pauses? VT?), against which reference standard, in which population, and — critically — **algorithm output or physician over-read?** An undefined accuracy metric cannot be substantiated and is misleading by vagueness.
- If the figures come from a published study, § 6 Nr. 3 HWG requires author, date and source **in the advertisement itself**. "On request" does not cure that. Fachkreise status does not exempt you; the professional reader is precisely who is entitled to verify.

Either state the claim properly or delete it. Offering data on request as *medical information* is fine; using the offer as an *advertising claim* is the issue.

**3. Latent intended-purpose conflict.** Your intended purpose is *recording* "for the detection of" — the detection sits with the HCP. Quoting device-level sensitivity/specificity implies an automated detection function. If the certified purpose does not cover an on-device detection algorithm, that claim is off-purpose regardless of how it is worded. Resolve this before drafting the replacement line.

---

## Should fix

**4. "up to 14 days" needs substantiation, and "bis zu" is scrutinised in DE.** German case law is unfriendly to maximum-value claims where the typical result is materially lower. If median adhesive wear time is 7–10 days, "bis zu 14 Tage" is exposed. Confirm (a) the figure matches the IFU, (b) it is covered by the current certificate, (c) what proportion of patients actually reach it. Consider adding a typical value.

**5. "continuous" dropped.** Minor, but it is in the intended purpose and costs nothing to restore.

**6. No single-lead limitation stated.** MDR Art. 7(d) prohibits creating a false impression by omitting likely risks/limitations. The bar is lower for Fachkreise, but one line ("Einkanal-Ableitung; kein Ersatz für ein 12-Kanal-EKG") is cheap insurance.

**7. Product name, manufacturer, and an IFU pointer.** Presumably in the layout, but they are not in the copy you sent. "Gebrauchsanweisung beachten" is standard practice.

---

## Check

**8. The Fachkreise gate must actually hold** (§ 2 HWG). Cardiology trade press qualifies. If the same creative is reused on an open website, LinkedIn or a non-gated digital edition, § 11 HWG applies and this copy would need reworking. (§ 12 / Anlage A is not a problem — cardiac disease was removed from that list in 2012.)

**9. Translation is the version that gets judged.** Use the registered German intended-purpose wording verbatim. "Erkennung" or "Detektion" — never "Diagnose". Note the German-language requirement in § 8 MPDG governs labelling/IFU rather than advertising, but an English ad in German trade press is harder to defend as non-misleading to its readership.

---

## Revised copy

**EN:**
> [Product] — continuous single-lead ECG recording in adults, under the supervision of a healthcare professional, for the detection of cardiac arrhythmias. Wear time up to 14 days (typical: [X] days). Single-lead recording; not a substitute for a 12-lead ECG. Please observe the instructions for use. [Manufacturer] · CE [NB no.]

**DE:**
> [Produkt] — kontinuierliche Einkanal-EKG-Aufzeichnung bei Erwachsenen unter Aufsicht von medizinischem Fachpersonal zur Erkennung von Herzrhythmusstörungen. Tragedauer bis zu 14 Tage (typisch: [X] Tage). Einkanal-Ableitung; kein Ersatz für ein 12-Kanal-EKG. Gebrauchsanweisung beachten. [Hersteller] · CE [Benannte Stelle]

**If you keep an accuracy claim**, replace item 2 with a cited, specific sentence:
> In [Autor et al., Journal Jahr] erkannte [Algorithmus/Auswertung] Vorhofflimmern bei [n] Erwachsenen mit einer Sensitivität von X % und einer Spezifität von Y % gegenüber [Referenzstandard].

---

## Open questions for the client

1. Does the certificate/IFU cover an on-device detection algorithm, or is detection purely the HCP's act?
2. Is 14 days the IFU-stated maximum wear time, and what is the observed median?
3. Are the sensitivity/specificity data published or internal clinical evaluation data?
4. What is the exact registered German intended-purpose wording?

This is a regulatory copy review, not legal advice — have your DE counsel or the Wettbewerbszentrale-experienced reviewer confirm before placement.

## Verdict

Directionally sound — no off-label claim, no superlatives, no comparatives. But three things would not survive a regulatory review as written.

---

## Must fix

**1. The population restriction "in adults" has been dropped.**
Your intended purpose is limited to adults. The copy says "Single-lead ECG recording for up to 14 days" with no population. Omitting a restriction from the intended purpose is exactly the kind of scope creep MDR Art. 7 catches — it implies the device is usable in paediatrics. Restore "bei Erwachsenen / in adults."

**2. "Sensitivity and specificity data available on request" is the biggest exposure.**
This is a performance reference without a verifiable source. Two problems:

- **HWG §6** — advertising that refers to studies or scientific data must name the author, title, date of publication and source. HWG §6 applies to Fachkreise advertising too (the Fachkreise carve-outs sit in §11/§12, not §6). "On request" satisfies none of it.
- **HWG §3 / MPDG §14 / UWG §5a** — the sentence creates the impression of proven favourable performance while withholding the figures the reader would need to judge it. That is the classic misleading-by-omission pattern.

Either state the numbers with a full citation, or delete the sentence. There is no compliant middle position.

**Scope trap in the same sentence:** if your sensitivity/specificity data are for **atrial fibrillation** (as is typical for patch ECG), you cannot present them under a general "cardiac arrhythmias" claim. The data must match the claim's breadth, or the claim narrows to match the data.

**3. "up to 14 days" is a new claim not in the intended purpose.**
Permissible if — and only if — 14 days is the maximum wear time stated in your IFU and is backed by adhesion and signal-quality data in the technical documentation. If the IFU says something lower, or says 14 days only under specified skin-prep/conditions, the unqualified "up to 14 days" is non-compliant. Verify against the IFU, don't assume.

---

## Also worth addressing

- **Language.** German trade press, German market. English copy isn't itself unlawful, but any regulatory-mandated content should be German, and a German-language ad is the defensible default.

## Findings

Intended purpose says **"in adults."** The copy omits it. That silently broadens the apparent indication to include paediatric use, which is a deviation from the registered intended purpose and is exactly what **MDR Art. 7** targets (text that misleads regarding intended purpose, performance, or indications). ### 2. "Sensitivity and specificity data available on request" (hold — highest risk)

Three problems stacked:

- **Unqualified diagnostic-accuracy claim.** Sensitivity/specificity *for what?* AF, pauses, AV block, VT and SVT have wildly different performance profiles. An undifferentiated claim across "cardiac arrhythmias" is scientifically meaningless and, to a cardiology readership, reads as a claim of validated accuracy across the whole class. - **"On request" is not a citation.** **§6 HWG** requires that where advertising references studies or expert findings, the source be stated precisely and reproduced faithfully. A promise to supply data later doesn't satisfy that, and it doesn't cure the claim made in the ad itself.
- **Burden of proof sits with you.** Settled BGH case law on health-related advertising reverses the burden: you must be able to show the claim rests on *gesicherte wissenschaftliche Erkenntnis*. Not wrong on its face, but it isn't in the intended purpose as given, so it has to come from the IFU and technical documentation. Check:

- Does the IFU actually specify a 14-day maximum wear time, or is 14 days a best-case lab figure? German courts read *"bis zu"* as implying the maximum is realistically attainable in normal use, not under ideal conditions.

The copy tracks the intended purpose correctly ("recording… for the detection"), so this is fine as written. But if the device ships an automated arrhythmia-detection algorithm, note that *algorithm* performance is a separate claim requiring its own substantiation, and the copy must not drift into implying the device diagnoses autonomously. ## What you correctly get to keep

Audience is Fachkreise, so **§11 HWG** (the restrictive catalogue — testimonials, case histories, depictions in professional dress, etc.) does not apply. Cardiac arrhythmias are not in the Anlage zu §12 HWG. You have more latitude here than consumer copy, so don't over-sanitise. **§3, §5, §6 HWG and the UWG apply in full regardless of audience.**

- [ ] 14-day wear time confirmed against IFU and wear-time validation data
- [ ] Sens/spec figures tied to a named arrhythmia, reference standard, and population
- [ ] "In adults" restored
- [ ] Legal manufacturer identified in the full ad layout; CE status stated accurately (MDR vs. Art. 120 legacy — don't imply MDR if you're on a legacy certificate)
